newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares shrug off usual summer lethargy.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares shrug off usual summer lethargy.

text.p: Russian equities are breaking records and bucking traditional summer doldrums, and a number of analysts said on Wednesday shares could breeze through August on local support before rising to new records in the autumn.
But some said that local demand in a market dominated by Western investors could fade and trigger a correction in August, usually one of the Russia's quietest months.

Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette investment bank chief economist for emerging markets Charles Blitzer saw investors bullish on news of a rouble redenomination next year and recent sales of stakes in telecoms holding company Svyazinvest and metals producer Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS.
"Basically I think the market will continue to move up in August," he said.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose 1.5 percent to close at its second record in two days, 533.86, on Wednesday.
One Western analyst saw the market steadying on low volumes by the end of the week with the RTS index around 520 to 525 for most of August.
"You are not seeing such a big marking down as you used to see," the analyst said. "Volumes may well come off but you won't see so much downward pressure when that happens."
"I think the main move will come in the fourth quarter," the analyst said, adding the market would rise another 10 to 15 percent by the middle of October.

Analysts said Russian investors were buying more actively than earlier this year as yields from the government securities market fell ever lower. Yields are below 20 percent versus nearly 200 percent in the middle of last year.
But Troika Dialog head of research Gavin Rankin said some leading energy utility shares were rising too far too fast.
"If Russian investors continue to push it higher we could probably expect to see a correction," Rankin said, declining to predict how far the market could ease.
Another analyst said prices could correct by up to 20 percent before resuming their climb.
Analysts disagreed whether any correction on Wall Street, feared by some investors edgy over a sky-high Dow Jones, would hit Russian stocks.

"If there is a major correction in the U.S., that will reverberate on all stock markets," said Blitzer. "At this point I would expect that a correction would reverberate less in Russia than in other places."
The Western analyst disagreed, however, saying markets were distinctive.

"People who watch the Dow Jones are not in Russia yet and those who are, are not buying for current year performance," the analyst said. "You are more insulated because your time horizon is different."
But by autumn Western investors were seen pouring new funds into Russia as its inclusion on the influential International Finance Corporation investable composite index in November approached.
Troika's Rankin added that more companies would announce foreign-trading American Depositary Receipts and Eurobonds which would also draw eyes towards the market at a time when it usually rallied.
"Certainly there will be more attention focused on the Russian market," he said.
